questions.prompt: Ditch model, eps = 0.05, q = 0, T = 20. Expected steps off the path? (two decimals)
Which assumption does behaviour cloning violate when the learner acts in a closed loop?
options: The actions to imitate are continuous values
The loss used for imitation is differentiable
Training and test states come from the same distribution
questions.explanation: The learner's own actions shape its states, so the test distribution differs from the demonstrations.

questions.prompt: eps = 0.05. Smallest horizon T for which the probability of at least one mistake exceeds 50% (integer)?
questions.skillLabel: Find the horizon for likely failure

questions.prompt: A DAgger implementation adds (s, learner.act(s)) for every state visited by the learner. What happens?
options: The new data reinforce the current policy, so there is no improvement at the new states
The data become off-policy, so the labels can no longer be used for supervised training
The learner converges faster, because the data now lie on exactly its own state distribution
The expert is queried twice for every state, which doubles the labelling cost of the data
questions.explanation: The labels are the learner's own outputs; the expert's knowledge never enters.

questions.prompt: eps = 0.04, q = 0.16. Steady-state off-path probability? (two decimals)
Demonstrations go around an obstacle on the left or the right equally often. A regression policy trained with squared error will
options: always go left, since it breaks the tie in a fixed way
become more accurate and avoid it as more data are added
choose the more common of the two sides and go around it
predict the average action and drive into the obstacle
questions.explanation: The mean of two modes is a third action that neither demonstrator takes.

questions.prompt: Policy A has 99.5% held-out one-step accuracy and 60% closed-loop success; policy B has 98% and 85%. Which statement is best supported?
options: B is better at the task; accuracy does not rank closed-loop performance
Accuracy is the only reliable metric for imitation policies
A is better, because its one-step accuracy is higher
They are equal, because both exceed 95% accuracy
questions.explanation: Closed-loop success measures the task, and it can invert the ranking by accuracy because of compounding and recovery behaviour.
